title: Absolute cohomological dimension for a profinite family of geometric proper fibres
statement:
Fix a prime $\ell$, an algebraic closure $\Omega=\overline{\mathbf Q}_\ell$, a finite subextension $E/\mathbf Q_\ell$, and a finite commutative ring $A$ killed by a power of $\ell$. Let $\Lambda\in\{A,\mathbf Z_\ell,\mathcal O_E,\mathbf Q_\ell,E,\Omega\}$, with the discrete topology for $A$ and the induced $\ell$-adic topology otherwise [sk-def-localizing-closure]. Its condensed ring uses all continuous maps from profinite sets, including when $\Lambda=\Omega$. For a scheme $T$ put $\Lambda_T=p_T^*\Lambda$ and $\mathcal A_T=\operatorname{Mod}_{\Lambda_T}$, using ordinary uncompleted module-object derived categories [sk-def-sfb-module-derived-pushpull] and the small-site/indexing universe [def-weil-size-convention]. Let $\mathcal P_T$ be the intersection of all replete classes in $\mathcal A_T$ containing zero and all finite constant scalar-model constructible modules [sk-def-sfb-constructible], closed under kernels and cokernels of maps between members, extensions, and all small ambient coproducts. Extension closure means that in $0\to M'\to M\to M''\to0$ membership of both ends implies membership of the middle. 
Let $C$ be an affine reduced zero-dimensional w-contractible scheme all of whose residue fields are separably closed [sk-def-pe-wlocal]; zero-dimensional here means that every prime of its affine coordinate ring is maximal. Let $h:Z\to C$ be proper [def-weil-proper-morphism], and let $e\geq0$ be an integer such that for every geometric point $\bar c:\operatorname{Spec}K\to C$, with $K$ algebraically closed, the fibre $Z_{\bar c}=Z\times_C\operatorname{Spec}K$ has topological Krull dimension at most $e$ [def-weil-geometric-fibre, def-kun-topological-krull-dimension]. Then for every $N\in\mathcal P_Z$,
$$H^r\bigl(R\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},N)\bigr)=0\qquad(r>2e+2).$$
Here $R\Gamma$ is the ordinary right derived global-section functor of $\mathcal A_Z$, valued in $D(\mathbf{Ab})$, and $N$ is placed in degree zero. The same numerical bound works for all such $N$, including arbitrary small coproducts and kernels and cokernels between their members. No Noetherianity, finite presentation of $h$, invertibility of $\ell$, derived completeness, or finite-subextension-valued replacement of the norm topology is assumed. The empty $C$ and empty fibres are included.

proof.text: The definition of properness says that $h$ is separated and of finite type. Fix an affine open $j:V\hookrightarrow Z$. Restrict a finite-type affine coordinate cover for $h$ to $V$, and refine by principal affine opens. This gives local finite type for $h\circ j$. Because both $V$ and $C$ are affine, this morphism is quasi-compact, so it is of finite type. Its geometric fibre is the open subspace $V_{\bar c}\subseteq Z_{\bar c}$. Dimension cannot increase on an open subspace: taking closures in the ambient space sends a strict chain of irreducible closed subsets to a strict chain, since intersecting back with the subspace recovers the original chain. Hence every geometric fibre of $V\to C$ has dimension at most the same $e$.

proof.text: Restriction $j^*$ sends $\mathcal P_Z$ into $\mathcal P_V$. The actual module inverse image is additive and exact, so it preserves zero, kernels, cokernels and short exact sequences. Its adjunction to module direct image implies preservation of the prescribed small ambient coproducts. A finite constant scalar-model stratification restricts to one on $V$: intersect each stratum and each local-model covering with $V$; restriction keeps the very same finitely presented scalar module in the local model. Thus it preserves the constructible generators as well. The inverse-image class $\{M\mid j^*M\in\mathcal P_V\}$ is replete and has every closure property in the defining intersection for $\mathcal P_Z$. Its minimality gives the assertion. This is a statement about membership; it does not assume that a cohomological vanishing class is closed under kernels.

proof.text:
Take any $N\in\mathcal P_Z$. For each affine open $V\subseteq Z$, Step 1 supplies the finite-type affine $V\to C$ and the fibre-dimension bound $e$, while Step 2 gives $j^*N\in\mathcal P_V$. Apply the affine Artin-type estimate to obtain
$$H^qR\Gamma(V_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},j^*N)=0\qquad(q>e+2).$$
The hypotheses on the base $C$ and all coefficient topologies are unchanged. The affine input applies to this whole closure class; no reduction of the norm-topological $\Omega$ to a finite coefficient extension or replacement by completed modules is used.

proof.text:
Apply the coefficient-independent affine-to-global lemma to $B=C$, $X=Z$, $g=h$, $\mathcal R=\Lambda_Z$, $M=N$, and $a=e+2$. Properness supplies separatedness and finite type as required; the base is affine and zero-dimensional and its geometric fibres satisfy the given bound. The affine-open hypothesis is exactly Step 3. Open restriction there is the module inverse image $j^*$ under the ringed open-slice comparison, so it is the restriction used by the lemma. The conclusion is
$$H^rR\Gamma(Z_{\mathrm{pro\acute et}},N)=0\qquad(r>e+(e+2)=2e+2).$$
Both inputs include the empty scheme, so this also covers empty $C$, empty $Z$, and empty affine opens. The choice of $e+2$ is independent of $N$ and of the affine open.
